Class OrderService

java.lang.Object
com.andreibel.server.services.OrderService
public class OrderService extends Object
Application service responsible for managing restaurant orders and computing availability.

This service is the transactional boundary for all order-related operations. It delegates persistence to repositories (OrderRepository, TableRepository, OpenTimeRepository) block to ensure a valid JDBC Connection is available.

Responsibilities

  • Create and query orders (CRUD-like operations).
  • Update order state: arrived (check-in), completed, cancelled.
  • Compute available reservation start times for a given date and party size.

Availability model

  • Reservation duration is fixed to 120 minutes (2 hours).
  • Reservations can start only on discrete time slots of size intervalMin (configured in OpenTime).
  • Restaurant opening and closing times are determined per date: first by a special-day record (OpenTimeRepository.findSpecial(Date)), otherwise by a regular/default record (OpenTimeRepository.findRegular()).
  • Table inventory is modeled as a mapping: capacity -> quantity.
  • A slot is considered available if the system can allocate tables for all currently active orders at each "change point" inside the reservation window plus the requested new party.

Allocation strategy

Table allocation uses a greedy strategy: sort groups by size descending, then for each group pick the smallest table capacity that can fit the group (via TreeMap.ceilingKey(Object)), skipping capacities whose remaining quantity is zero.

Thread-safety

The class is implemented as a simple lazy Singleton without synchronization. If multiple threads may call getInstance() concurrently, consider synchronizing the initialization or using an enum/safe singleton pattern.

      Creates a new order in the database.

      Transactional write operation:

      1. Maps OrderRequest to a new Order entity.
      2. Persists the entity via OrderRepository.save(Order).

    • deleteOrder

      public com.andreibel.message.DTO.OrderResponse deleteOrder(UUID conformationCode)
      Cancels (soft-deletes) an order by its confirmation code.

      Transactional write operation:

      1. Updates the row via OrderRepository.deleteByConformationCode(java.util.UUID) (typically sets orderCancelled = 1).
      2. Re-reads the updated order via OrderRepository.findByConformationCode(java.util.UUID).
      3. Maps the updated entity to OrderResponse.

      Parameters:
      conformationCode - confirmation code identifying the order to cancel
      Returns:
      updated (cancelled) order as DTO

    • getAllAvailableTimeInDate

      public List<LocalTime> getAllAvailableTimeInDate(LocalDate date, int numberOfGuests)
      Computes all available reservation start times for a given date and party size.

      The returned list includes only start times t such that:

      • t is within the restaurant working hours for that date,
      • t + 2 hours does not exceed closing time,
      • for each "change point" within the reservation window (every intervalMin minutes), the existing active orders plus the new party can be allocated to the available tables.

      Data sources

      • Opening hours and interval from OpenTimeRepository (special-day first, otherwise regular).
      • Table inventory from TableRepository.findAll().
      • All orders starting on the requested date from OrderRepository.findAllDateOrders(LocalDate).

      Algorithm (high level)

      1. Resolve working hours and slot interval for the given date.
      2. Build a capacity inventory map: capacity -> quantity.
      3. Generate candidate start slots from open time up to the last possible start time.
      4. For each slot, validate availability using isSlotAvailable(LocalDateTime, int, List, TreeMap, int, int).
      Parameters:
      date - calendar date to compute availability for
      numberOfGuests - requested party size
      Returns:
      list of available start times as LocalTime (can be empty)
